headline: Corrected HHJK (2019) post-2010 extension: the ABSOLUTE contribution of falling frictions to market-GDP-per-person growth was 0.04 pp/yr in 2000-2010 and 0.06 pp/yr in 2010-2023 under BOTH deflator conventions (not slowing); the SHARE (L4) is deflator-sensitive — 7.0% paper / 5.2% corrected, paired with L4b 7.3% / 29.2% — and Gate 3b FAILED its pre-registered earnings tolerance under every route.

figures.caption: Earnings-weighted mean composite friction tau-hat by group, 1960-2023, rebuilt from the paper's Octave estimator (solid/diamond) with the prior Python values overlaid (dotted x). The correction is largest for Black women in 1960 (7.90 -> 6.69). The 2010->2023 segment is dashed (12-year step).
figures.alt: Three decaying curves (white women, Black men, Black women) for mean tau-hat from 1960 toward the white-men reference of 1; faint dotted prior-Python points sit above the corrected Octave curve for Black women in early years.

figures.caption: Why L4 looks deflator-sensitive. Left: the SHARE of growth from falling tau swings with the deflator (L4b 7.3% -> 29.2%) because the corrected 2010 deflator compresses 2000-2010 actual growth. Right: the ABSOLUTE friction contribution (0.04 and 0.06 pp/yr) is identical under both conventions. Only the denominator moves.
figures.alt: Two bar panels: left shows shares diverging between paper and corrected deflators (especially 2000-10); right shows the absolute pp/yr contributions equal under both conventions.

notes: A FAILED gate is reported FAILED. Gate 3b failed its own pre-registered earnings-level tolerance under every route; the prior 'semantic PASS' category does not exist in the spec. The 2023 results are retained via the spec's honest-partial path, with the consequence quantified: the level convention moves L4 within 6.1-8.4% (L5 invariant at 9.0) and never approaches the ~40% historical share. The out-of-trigger 2010-2012 3-year PUMS fetch is disclosed (two tolerances were failing, not population-shares-only).

Completed dropped deliverables: LivingDefl L6 (2010-23 WW/BM/BW = 3.8/0.5/0.8), filled group_shares.csv, L7 (WW tau 2023: doctors 1.01, lawyers 1.04, construction 6.33, secretaries 0.38), L2 young relative-propensity SD, L8 earnings/worker + LFP data-vs-model 2023 (64080/60918; 0.792/0.790), L9 annual relative-propensity SD 2017-19 & 2021-24. robustness_summary.csv columns relabeled to the true tauH-only/tauW-only shares (prior held Ywkr/Cons). R4 relabeled an argmax-split proxy (differs from the modal map in only 5 of 538 codes).

Stability (gate 7): raw per-occupation tau-hat for 1960-2010 is identical between the 6- and 7-period runs (max rel 4.6e-16, identical finite-cell pattern), so the masked GetTExperience re-run is moot; the 1.6-2.7% mean-tau-hat shifts are a pure earningsweights_avg reweighting. The headline SHARE estimands are stable: 1960->2010 L3=41.3 (vs 41.5), L6 WW/BM/BW=33.6/1.2/3.7 (vs 33.8/1.2/3.7), all <=0.2 pp.

003 theory corrections (results/003_theory_corrections.md): tauW is NOT flat for white women (47% of their 2010-23 decline; 51% under R5) — only flat for Black men and minor for Black women; the Hurst-Rubinstein-Shimizu paraphrase is corrected (flat adjusted gap EVEN AS discrimination fell); [PROJECTED, conditional] tags added to the headline projection and the ~8.8%-unrealised metric; the projection carries no forecast power for white women (backtest error 0.193 >> the projected 0.049 ln-tau decline), so the ~0.08%/decade sits inside the law's own error band; the continued/slowed cut-off is the study's own post-hoc choice (white women borderline at 0.341 vs 1/3); the forward 0.0075%/yr is now also compared with the measured 2010-23 ~0.06%/yr, not only 1960-2010.

Reuses 001/002/003 .mat files and the staged Octave stage-split tooling; foreground only; no installs/fetches. Octave figures stubbed with no-op graphics shims (gnuplot unavailable, installs forbidden); numeric invariance verified. Longest Octave stage ~283 s (< 540 s backstop).
